lyrics:
[Intro: solo piano, plain hymn-like chords]

[Verse 1: warm, close, piano only]
When the night has got its hands on me
And every little thing is wrong
I can hear my grandmother at the sink
Humming her one song

[Chorus: soft choir joins, bass enters]
Leave it till morning, leave it till morning
The dark makes it bigger than it is
Leave it till morning, child
It'll keep, it'll keep

[Verse 2: drums enter gently, organ]
And when the worried people of the world agree
On nothing but the worry and the fear
There's a kettle going somewhere, there's a light
And somebody saying "here"

[Chorus: choir fuller, organ]
Leave it till morning, leave it till morning
The dark makes it bigger than it is
Leave it till morning, child
It'll keep, it'll keep

[Guitar Solo: warm, melodic, over the chorus chords]

[Verse 3: full band, voice stronger]
And when the morning comes, if it's still there
We'll look at it together in the light
Most of what was howling at the door
Was only the night

[Final Chorus: choir at full voice, handclaps, ad-libs]
Leave it till morning, leave it till morning
The dark makes it bigger than it is
Leave it till morning, child
It'll keep, it'll keep
Leave it till morning
It'll keep

[Outro: piano alone, a tap running, a hummed line]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 72 BPM, 4/4, C major. A slow, steady hymn. Calm, plain and consoling.

VOICE: Male tenor, warm and unforced, singing as if to one person. A gospel-style choir of mixed voices enters softly at the first chorus and grows to full strength by the last, with handclaps and improvised lines. A hummed tune at the very end.

INSTRUMENTS: A piano playing simple, church-like chords. A Hammond-style organ. Electric bass. A drum kit that enters gently in verse 2. A lead electric guitar with a warm, slightly overdriven tone for a melodic solo. The choir. Small domestic sounds at the close.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano. 0:13 Verse 1. 0:40 Chorus 1, choir and bass. 1:07 Verse 2, drums and organ. 1:34 Chorus 2. 2:01 Guitar solo. 2:28 Verse 3. 2:55 Final chorus with the choir at full voice. 3:30 Outro, piano alone, a tap running and a hummed line, ending at 3:48.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Around 1970, a band recorded live with a choir added: warm, simple and roomy, piano and voice central.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The choir's first entry on the chorus at 0:40.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The advice is ordinary and tested: problems look bigger at night. Verse 3 keeps the promise by looking at the trouble in daylight, together, which the original's three words leave open.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Night fear, comfort, daylight.
